chapter: Billy Hicks, the Apollo and Roy Eldridge
title: Joining Roy's band and being christened Panama
summary: His first week with Roy, the hat prompted the name Panama, which stuck; only people who knew him before 1939 call him David.

story.theme_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band monikers
story.community_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band names

blocks.x: But I had this job lined up with Roy Eldridge, and so I joined his band, like, the first week in

July, and that's when my name was changed from David to Panama. That's the reason when I meet someone that calls me David right now, it's someone that knew me before 1939. You know, you can always tell the people who knew me before 1939, because they would call me David, with the exception of a few musicians, one outstanding, and that's my boy, Binks "Dizzy" Gillespie; he calls me David, and he never called me Panama.

Calls you John? Well, he calls me David and never calls me Panama. But he's one of the few people that I met later on, after 1939 that called me David. Everybody else calls me Panama, and how I got this name was my first day in the band with Roy, we were at rehearsal, and something happened - and I still couldn't read now; I was still playing by ear, but nobody knew it because like I say, drop that stick in a minute, and listen to what's going on while I'm looking for the stick, you know -- so anyway, something happened; I did something wrong, I guess, but anyway, Roy turns to me, because I had on my Panama hat, I was sitting up there because I figured I wasn't gonna stay there long anyway, because I had just come from Florida, you know, and here I am with Roy Eldridge and I don't think I'm gonna make it, see, so I had my hat on, all ready to leave, you know, if anything should happen, and he turns to me and says, "Hey Panama!" -- and the guys in the band thought this was my name, and I was too scared to tell them it wasn't, so it stuck. So that's how I got the name
